scope: Author planning-model syntax/render consistency;not executable regression tests,ACL seals,native repair or independent acceptance.

scenarios.description: fatal failure with a prepared unpublished request

steps.text: a RequestLease in PreparedUnpublished holding a ResourceLease
CleanupStarted disables normal producers
the request is proven unpublished and becomes AbandonedUnpublished
cleanup does not flush that application SQE
the ResourceLease is released only after all other retaining requests retire

scenarios.description: enter fails after shared SQ tail publication

steps.text: a RequestLease made Published before io_uring_enter
enter reports an error during fatal unwind
the lease remains Published or PublicationUncertain, never PreparedUnpublished
its ResourceLease remains live until correlated TerminalCompletion

scenarios.description: drain pending one-shot operations without restarting HTTP work

steps.text: published RequestLease instances for ACCEPT, RECV, heap READ and SEND
CleanupStarted disables normal completion callbacks and rearming
cleanup consumes each correlated TerminalCompletion without producing HTTP work
each ResourceLease stays live through every retaining target retirement
only then can CleanupSettled permit deferred resource destruction

scenarios.description: cancellation receipt is not target acknowledgment

steps.text: a published RequestLease with an unread target completion or an unresolved target
a CancellationReceipt reports success, a nonnegative count or no match
only separately observed TerminalCompletion establishes TargetRetired; it is not consumed twice
no control tag or submit count substitutes for TargetRetired

scenarios.description: failed timed-out or noncancelable target preserves ownership

steps.text: an unresolved published RequestLease retaining application memory
cancellation fails, times out or cannot retire the target
CleanupStalled preserves the ResourceLease and access to outstanding results
cleanup does not return through defers that free referenced memory
the verifier requires an explicit safe escalation policy before acceptance

scenarios.description: successful ACCEPT completion remains unread during fatal cleanup

steps.text: an ACCEPT TerminalCompletion in ReadyUnread with a nonnegative descriptor
cleanup drains that completion despite cancel no-match
AcceptDescriptorClaimed creates a ResourceLease and ResourceReleased closes it
owned peer EOF and whole descriptor census are observed before process exit

scenarios.description: copied acknowledged ACCEPT result has not reached a client owner

steps.text: an ACCEPT result in CopiedUndispatched after CQ advancement
fatal cleanup starts before the result is transferred to a ClientSlot
cleanup claims and releases its ResourceLease exactly once
an empty CQ or copied-result discard cannot substitute for release

scenarios.description: descriptor zero is a successful ACCEPT resource

steps.text: an ACCEPT TerminalCompletion whose result is descriptor zero
cleanup claims successful resource results
descriptor zero receives a ResourceLease and is closed exactly once
zero is not classified as EOF or a failed ACCEPT

scenarios.description: idle phase does not erase an already claimed accepted descriptor

steps.text: a ClientSlot still in idle owns an accepted ResourceLease
configuration fails before reception is queued
cleanup releases that owned descriptor despite the idle phase
phase filtering cannot discard descriptor ownership

scenarios.description: cleanup control admission respects a finite SQ

steps.text: up to thirty-three unresolved application leases and a requested sixty-four-entry SQ
cleanup needs up to thirty-three cancellation requests
control admission accounts for remaining SQ occupancy, not just controller count
cleanup does not assume all sixty-six application and control entries fit at once
backpressure or admission failure cannot trigger early operand release

scenarios.description: fatal observer output failure with a late loopback peer

steps.text: an idle receiver and next ACCEPT are published while another response is active
observer output fails and a late peer connects
cleanup retires published requests and claims every successful ACCEPT resource
pre-exit census and peer EOF prove cleanup, not operating-system process exit

scenarios.description: normal partial I/O and per-client errors remain unchanged

steps.text: CleanupSession is inactive during normal HTTP operation
a request fragments, SEND completes short or a peer abandons its response
whole wire bytes and per-client progress preserve the existing public contracts
another client can finish while one client waits
normal producer rearming remains enabled outside fatal cleanup
